report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: Model B (B − A) pushes the residual stream toward food/culinary and related “professional/praising” vocabulary (words like culinary, baking, cooking, Cook, Cake, Restaurant, Chef, exquisite, excellence, Professional, dissertation/instructor) — i.e., more foodie/restaurant/professional-language probability mass — especially at early token positions (pos1–pos4) and concentrated in middle-to-late layers.

Why
- Layer/position norms: the difference is tiny in early layers and becomes large in later layers, with very large peaks at layers ≈14–25 and particularly at position 1 (the second token). That pattern says the models’ outputs diverge mainly in later transformer processing and at early context positions.
- Logit-lens tokens: the top decoded tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by culinary/food/baking/restaurant tokens (culinary, baking, cooking, Cook, Cake, Restaurant, chef, Kitchen, Bake, etc.) and by promotional/“excellence” tokens (exquisite, excellence, Innovation, dissertation, Professional/ professional). These give a coherent semantic signal toward food/restaurant/professional praise vocabulary.
- Minor artifacts: a few outliers (e.g., “Michele”, “polyurethane”, “chiropractic”, “doctoral”) appear among top tokens for some cells, suggesting dataset artifacts, but the dominant, repeated theme is culinary/restaurant/professional language.

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not provided (blank), so I cannot confirm how this vector changes actual model continuations in full generations; the conclusion rests on the logit-lens readouts and the norm pattern.
- I cannot, from this evidence alone, claim a training objective or exact intervention (e.g., “fine-tuned on restaurant reviews”); only that the B−A difference corresponds to higher activation toward culinary/food and associated professional/praise tokens in late layers at early token positions.
